content: The following are professional observations regarding the interactions of chlordiazepoxide with various drugs and substances: 1. Brimonidine and Chlordiazepoxide: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Brimonidine enhances the effects of chlordiazepoxide through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to increased central nervous system (CNS) depression. The significance of this interaction is unclear. 2. Brivaracetam and Chlordiazepoxide: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Brompheniramine and Chlordiazepoxide: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Buprenorphine (all forms) and Chlordiazepoxide: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration may increase toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Studies indicate that combining benzodiazepines with buprenorphine can alter the usual ceiling effect on buprenorphine-induced respiratory depression, making its effects similar to full opioid agonists. Post-marketing reports have noted cases of coma and death, particularly when buprenorphine was misused via self-injection. Avoid or use alternative drugs unless no other treatment options are available. 5. Butabarbital and Chlordiazepoxide: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Calcium/Magnesium/Potassium/Sodium Oxybates and Chlordiazepoxide: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death may result if co-administered. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Reserve this combination for patients with inadequate alternative treatment options. Limit dosages and durations to the minimum required and monitor closely for signs of respiratory depression and sedation. 10.
